description_full: Kingsoft Cloud Holdings Limited provides cloud services to businesses and organizations primarily in China. The company's product portfolio includes cloud products, such as infrastructure as a service (IaaS) infrastructure, platform as a service (PaaS) middleware, software as a service (SaaS) applications, and AI solution. It offers research and development services, as well as enterprise digital solutions and related services. The company also provides public cloud services to customers in various verticals, including video, e-commerce, intelligent mobility, artificial intelligence, and mobile internet; and enterprise cloud services to customers in financial services, public service, and healthcare businesses. Kingsoft Cloud Holdings Limited was incorporated in 2012 and is headquartered in Beijing, China.

financial_summary: Kingsoft Cloud Holdings Limited is a mid-cap technology business with a $2.6B market cap on $1.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +3% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

Returns on capital run at -29% against a 11% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 9% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
Accruals are elevated at -17.7% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.2× net debt/EBITDA, and thin -1.6× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Net dilution runs at 26.7% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.0× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
